To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of machine learning methods based on observations of solar coronal holes in combination with the predicted values of the solar wind speed at Earth's orbit allows to improve the accuracy of medium-term forecasting of the integral daily flux (fluence) of relativistic electron (RE, E > 2 MeV ) in a geostationsary orbit.

the accuracy of predicting the RE fluence three or four days in advance is increased by 10–15% when adding to the input parameters the predicted values of the solar wind speed at Earth's orbit obtained by processing images from AIA/SDO.
the accuracy of predicting the integral daily RE fluence in a geostationsry orbit can be increased by adding the predicted values ​​of solar wind speed to the input parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model that predicts the fluxes of relativistic electrons of the Earth's radiation belt in the geostationary orbits using the data on solar activity and the solar wind.
the prediction of RE fluxes in geostationary orbits, and the results show that the proposed model can be used for the prediction of RE in geostationery orbits with an acceptable accuracy.
the development of a new forecasting method for the RE fluences based on the machine learning approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed model of forecasting the RE fluences in the geostationary Earth orbit, based on the images of solar coronal holes, is a promising approach for predicting the fluxes of high-energy particles in the Earth's radiation belt.
the proposed method of predicting the RE fluxes in a geostationsary orbit is promising and requires further development and improvement.

the proposed method of predicting the integral daily RE fluences in the geostationary orbits based on observations of coronal holes on the Sun is a promising approach for the development of a forecasting system of the radiation environment in near-Earth space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of machine learning methods for predicting relativistic electron fluxes based on the observations of solar coronal holes and solar wind speed is a promising approach for space weather forecasting.
the use of solar wind data, obtained from the analysis of the Sun images in UV range, allows us to improve the prediction of RE fluxes in a geostationsary orbit.
we have shown that the prediction of solar wind parameters and relativistic electron fluxes is possible with the help of a neural network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method of forecasting RE fluxes in a geostational orbit is more effective than the methods based on the solar wind speed at L1 point.
the proposed model can be used to predict the fluxes of relativistic electrons in geostationary orbits with a lead time of 3-4 days.

the prediction of RE fluxes in a geostationaly orbit is more accurate if we use the images of solar corona obtained in the ultraviolet spectral range, and not the solar wind data obtained by the in-situ measurements of the solar wind parameters in the Earth's orbit.
